This file exists because a decision that lives only in a chat log is not a
decision any session can check. On 2026-08-27 the drill/cue read policy was
ratified and written down nowhere. #754 merged the next day as `81e27e72`
carrying test expectations that asserted the opposite -- `board` admitted to
the drill library -- and `main` shipped code contradicting a ruling that had
already been made. Establishing *when* the ruling happened later took an hour
of forensics across PR bodies and commit timestamps, and produced only a
one-hour bracket, because the sole trace was an undated code comment on an
unmerged branch. That is the cost this file is here to stop paying.

## What belongs here

A decision the owner made that governs code, schema, policy, or how AI work is
done, where a session could otherwise build the opposite in good faith.
Jason's decisions are recorded only here, by Claude, quoting him
(OD-2026-09-28-003). That includes release decisions -- what was frozen,
refused, or abandoned. Until 2026-09-21 those were recorded in
`docs/current/AI_RELEASE_CONTROL.md`; that record is now in
`docs/archive/2026-09-21_AI_RELEASE_CONTROL_before_condense.md`. Release
procedure is `docs/AI_DELIVERY_PIPELINE.md`.

The index of rulings at the top is generated: every PR that adds an entry, or a
fixed-form `**Status, YYYY-MM-DD:**` line, must run
`node scripts/owner-decisions-index.mjs --write` and commit the result, or CI fails.

Not here: work assignments, scope for a single ticket, or anything a session
may decide for itself. `docs/current/ACTIVE_WORK.md` holds blocked and parked
work.

## How to use it

**Before writing a test, gate, or migration that asserts a policy, read this
file.** If the policy is here, or in a source listed under "Decisions recorded
elsewhere" below, build to it. If it is in neither and you need it
decided, say so and stop -- `AGENT_KERNEL.md` classifies that as
**OWNER DECISION REQUIRED**, and inventing the answer is the failure mode this
file was written after.

If code you are reading contradicts an entry here, that is a finding. Report
it. Do not assume the entry is stale.

## Decisions recorded elsewhere

Owner rulings that predate this file, or were written where the work happened,
still live in these places (index added 2026-09-28 from the documentation
review, finding F29). The source is the record; this list only says where to
look. When one of them governs new work, record it here as a new entry quoting
the source.

## Honesty rules for entries

These follow "Report the check, not the conclusion" in `AGENT_KERNEL.md`.

- **Quote the owner verbatim.** A paraphrase is an interpretation, and the
  interpretation is the thing that goes wrong. Where the words alone do not
  carry the decision -- "go with A" -- record what A was, as it was put to
  him, so the choice can be read without the surrounding conversation.
- **Mark provenance.** `PRIMARY` means the owner's own words are recorded
  here. `RECONSTRUCTED` means the text was recovered from an artifact written
  by someone else, and it says which artifact and what is uncertain.
- **Name the evidence the decision rested on**, with the run, PR or SHA that
  proves it. A decision made on a measurement that later changes is worth
  re-opening; one made on nothing is worth knowing about.
- **Record it at ratification, not at merge.** The gap between the two is
  exactly where #754 went wrong.
- **Do not edit a decision.** Supersede it with a new entry that says what it
  replaces and why. When later facts change what an entry reports, append a
  dated `Status (YYYY-MM-DD):` line under it; the decision text stays as
  written.
- **One id, once.** Before adding an entry, grep `## OD-<date>-` for the next
  free number. `scripts/check-owner-decision-ids.mjs` fails if a heading id
  repeats or is malformed; CI runs it on every change, docs-only included
  (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, "Check owner decision ids are unique").

Newest first.

## A pattern this file exists to shorten

Twice on 2026-08-28, `main` carried a test suite asserting the opposite of a
ruling the owner had already made, and in both cases an open PR was the
correction:

| ruling | `main` asserted the opposite in | corrected by | window |
|---|---|---|---|
| OD-2026-08-27-001 (board denied) | #754, merged `81e27e72` | #755, merged `61b20e9d` | ~75 minutes |
| OD-2026-08-28-005 (content class) | #811, merged `948f6d18` | #817 | open at time of writing |

Status (2026-09-28): #817 merged 2026-08-28 as `d08ca4dd`.

The two are not the same failure and should not be filed as one.

#754 is the one this file was written after. Its expectations were already
wrong when it merged, and nothing in the repository recorded the ruling that
made them wrong, so no session could have known.

#811 is the honest version. It was written BEFORE the ruling, its body said in
terms that the posture was open and unsettled, and its tests pinned the current
behaviour precisely so a change could not happen silently. Then the ruling
came, and the pin did exactly what a pin is for: it made the correction
explicit and reviewable instead of invisible.

**So a characterization test that merges and is then inverted is not a defect.**
The defect is a test that asserts a posture while claiming, in a comment, to
pin a decision it cannot detect a change to -- which is what #811 was itself
written to fix in two other files.

What this file can shorten is only the first shape: a session about to assert a
policy can now check whether one has been ruled. It cannot prevent the second,
and should not try to.

## OD-2026-11-17-012 -- The runner design is approved: fork-PR approval for all outside contributors, and staging uses the Azure runners too: "A: Approve as designed (Recommended)"; "A: All outside (Recommended)"; "A: Staging too (Recommended)"

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answers on the card, 2026-11-17T20:07:48.394Z (about 15:07 US Eastern), the tool result at transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/36c40fe1-f38b-4561-beab-f5f203db0c40.jsonl`, line 27205, checked against the card by script. The card is at line 27203 (2026-11-17T20:07:28.132Z). It builds on OD-2026-11-17-008, which is not edited. New; edits no earlier entry's text.

**What was put to him (the card at line 27203, quoted):**

> **Runner model**
> Question, as shown:
> Official: Lane DBT's design for OD-2026-11-17-008 (our own Azure runners): short-lived Container Apps jobs in the existing East US environment, about $5-10 a month (INFERRED). Each runner is single-use (GitHub's "JIT" kind), gets a random label, and is checked by a guard hook (main branch, dispatch or schedule, listed workflows only). It is started by a GitHub App whose permission ("Administration: write") is repo-admin-equivalent, because the repo is on a personal account, not an organization. The App key would live only in a dedicated Key Vault, never in GitHub secrets or the runner. GitHub advises against self-hosted runners on public repos; single-use runners are its stated mitigation. Approve this security model?
>
> Plain: To build our own Azure runners, a small GitHub 'robot' needs near-admin rights on the repo, and its key would sit locked in Azure. The design adds several safety layers. Go ahead, move the repo to a free GitHub organization first (narrower rights, more setup), or stop at the fast-fail check?
>
> Options, in the order shown:
> 1. "A: Approve as designed (Recommended)": Build it: three PRs, I create the Azure resources, you create the GitHub App and paste its key into Key Vault yourself. Pros: fixes every blocked job; no firewall change. Cons: a near-admin key exists (locked in Key Vault).
> 2. "B: Move to a GitHub org first": Create a free organization and move the repo, so runners can be limited to listed workflows and the App needs less power. Pros: narrower rights. Cons: more setup; Azure sign-in links and repo URLs change.
> 3. "C: Stop at the fast-fail check": No self-hosted runners. Blocked jobs fail fast with a clear message and I re-run them. Pros: no new key. Cons: manual re-runs at a rising rate.

> **Fork approval**
> Question, as shown:
> Official: Today the repo asks for approval before Actions run on pull requests from first-time contributors only (setting: first_time_contributors). The design recommends requiring approval for ALL outside contributors' pull requests, so no outside code can reach a workflow without your click. Change it?
>
> Plain: Make GitHub wait for your OK before running any outsider's code, not just first-timers'.
>
> Options, in the order shown:
> 1. "A: All outside (Recommended)": Approval required for every outside contributor's pull request. Pros: tighter. Cons: an extra click if outsiders ever contribute (none do today).
> 2. "B: Keep first-time only": Leave the setting as it is.

> **Staging too**
> Question, as shown:
> Official: 15 of the 19 production-database jobs also run against staging when dispatched with target=staging. Staging timed out 3 times in 14 days for the same reason. Should staging dispatches of those shared workflows also use the Azure runners (cost about nothing extra)?
>
> Plain: Use our own runners for staging runs too, or only for production?
>
> Options, in the order shown:
> 1. "A: Staging too (Recommended)": Same runners for both targets. Pros: staging stops timing out; one path to maintain. Cons: none material.
> 2. "B: Production only": Staging keeps GitHub's runners and occasional re-runs.

**Jason:** "A: Approve as designed (Recommended)"; "A: All outside (Recommended)"; "A: Staging too (Recommended)"

**Ruling:**

1. The security model for the own-Azure-runners design (single-use runners, a guard hook, a GitHub App started with repo-admin-equivalent rights, its key only in a dedicated Key Vault) is approved as designed. Jason creates the GitHub App and pastes its key himself (the card's option A).
2. Pull requests from all outside contributors need approval before Actions run.
3. Staging dispatches of the shared production-database workflows use the Azure runners too.
4. **Applied (REPORTED, Overwatch STATUS):** the fork-PR approval setting was changed to all outside contributors and verified by a read of the setting.

**Not ruled here:** the secret steps (the GitHub App, key, grant, guard check and pilot), deferred by OD-2026-11-18-003.

**Status:** recorded 2026-11-19 by PR.

## OD-2026-11-17-008 -- Production-database jobs move to short-lived self-hosted runners inside Azure (main branch only); a GitHub runner credential and usage-billed Azure resources are approved: "A"

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's typed reply "A", 2026-11-17 about 13:59 EST (transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/36c40fe1-f38b-4561-beab-f5f203db0c40.jsonl`, line 26419, 2026-11-17T18:59:52.951Z, `origin.kind` human), checked against the file by script before writing. Raised by lane DBT's step-1 report (`DBT_STEP1_REPORT.md`), whose cause Overwatch checked in the run logs before asking. New; edits no earlier entry's text.

**What was put to him (the card at line 26384, quoted):**

> Official: Lane DBT found the cause of today's production-database timeouts (OBSERVED in 276 runs over 30 days): GitHub now runs some jobs on AWS servers, and the database firewall admits only Azure addresses. AWS-runner database jobs: 7 of 7 timed out. Azure-runner jobs: 0 of 214. The AWS share is rising (13.8% of database jobs on 11-17). A code-only fast-fail check (no security change) is approved and being built. It turns each block into a clear error in about 20 seconds, but jobs that land on AWS still need a re-run. Which structural fix, if any? Cost note: new Azure resources are usage-billed; the exact cost is UNVERIFIED.
>
> Plain: Some of GitHub's robots now run outside Azure, and our database only lets Azure in, so about 1 in 7 runs gets blocked and has to be retried. Do we build our own robots inside Azure, add an automatic retry for the nightly jobs, open a temporary door for each run, or just keep retrying by hand?
>
> Options, in the order shown:
> 1. "A: Our own Azure runners (Recommended)": Short-lived self-hosted runners inside Azure (Container Apps jobs) for the production-database jobs only; main branch only, never PRs (the repo is public). New Azure resources and a GitHub runner-registration credential. Pros: fixes every job; a fixed address later lets us remove the 'allow all of Azure' rule, which tightens security. Cons: new resources to run and pay for; a new credential.
> 2. "B: Nightly jobs retry themselves": Scheduled jobs (backup, session close, cleanup) get a second daily run that skips if the first one worked; their token gains read access to Actions history. Pros: no new resources; missed nights heal. Cons: production releases, migrations and loads still need a manual re-run about 1 time in 7.
> 3. "C: Temporary door per run": Each job adds a firewall rule for its own address, then removes it. Pros: fixes every job. Cons: loosens security for those minutes; the deploy identity needs firewall-write rights; a killed job leaves the door open.
> 4. "D: Nothing more": Keep only the fast-fail check; I re-run blocked jobs by hand. Pros: no change. Cons: manual re-runs at a rising rate; missed nightly jobs stay missed.

**Jason:** *"A"* (read as the first option, "A: Our own Azure runners (Recommended)")

**Ruling:**

1. The production-database jobs run on short-lived self-hosted runners inside Azure (Container Apps jobs), main branch only, never pull requests (the repository is public).
2. New usage-billed Azure resources and a GitHub runner-registration credential are approved for this. Jason creates or enters the credential himself; Claude never handles its value.
3. The second-daily-run option (B) is not taken. The code-only fast-fail check approved by Overwatch under OD-2026-11-17-006 stays as a guard.

**Not ruled here:** the design itself (lane DBT reports it to Overwatch first; resource creation and the workflow switch are later steps); removing the allow-all-Azure firewall rule once the runners have a fixed address (a separate card).

**What was put to him (quoted, question 2 of the card):**

> Official: Three frozen adult templates (stages T1/T2/AM1/RC1 and up; no youth stage) give minutes for a controlled_sparring item: 'Phase 1 Foundation / Novice - Sparring session' 30 min, 'Phase 2 Competitive Amateur' constrained live 25 min, 'Session structure for skill development' 20 min. The app's template table refuses a duration on any contact above light_technical (check pilot_wti_no_contact_volume, Aug 2026: 'A qualified human sets contact volume, in person, every time'). How should those minutes load?
>
> Plain: Your Long Road sessions say how many minutes of sparring. The app has a rule that a template never presets sparring time, so the coach decides it on the day. Show your minutes as information, drop the rule, or leave the minutes out?
>
> Options, in the order shown:
> 1. "A: Show as info (Recommended)": Keep the rule. The minutes load as your text, labelled, shown beside the item, and are never used as a preset by timers or issuing. Pros: your content shows as written; the app never presets sparring time. Cons: minutes live in a note, not the duration field.
> 2. "B: Drop the rule": Minutes go in the duration field like any drill, and timers and issuing would use them. Pros: simplest. Cons: removes the rule that a coach sets contact volume in person.
> 3. "C: Leave minutes out": The sparring items load without minutes. Cons: part of your text is withheld (Backbone RULES s0).

**Jason:** *"A: Show as info (Recommended)"*

**Ruling:**

1. The check `pilot_wti_no_contact_volume` (workout-templates migration, "NO PRESCRIBED SPARRING VOLUME") stays unchanged.
2. Where a frozen template gives minutes for an item above `light_technical` (the 3 `controlled_sparring` items: 30, 25 and 20 minutes), the minutes load as the source's text in the item's details, labelled, with the duration column blank, and the template page shows them beside the item as information.

## OD-2026-11-17-001 -- Blank required fields on frozen session templates are AI-drafted, labelled and checked by the lane's two reviewers: "B: AI drafts the values"

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answer to a two-question card in the Claude Code session on the Overwatch account (transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/36c40fe1-f38b-4561-beab-f5f203db0c40.jsonl`): card at line 24368 (2026-11-17T13:23:33.647Z), answer at line 24369 (2026-11-17T13:27:10.960Z, about 08:27 EST; the `AskUserQuestion` result, which carries his picks), checked against the file by script before writing. Raised by lane YR's step-1 report (`YR_STEP1_REPORT.md`, sha256[:16] `f09b6153e6d5b9b1`, section 7), checked by Overwatch against the frozen Backbone and the workout-templates migration before it was put to him. New; edits no earlier entry's text.

**What was put to him (quoted, question 1 of the card):**

> Official: Lane YR (youth + recreational content) found 23 of 33 frozen session templates with blank required fields: session_type (23), difficulty (23), duration_minutes (13), intent (2). One template, 'The permanent circuit ... ~10 min', is 10 minutes, under the app's 15-minute floor. OD-2026-11-12-001 ('A: Load blanks') covered drill setup and steps only and left other fields unruled. How should these templates load?
>
> Plain: Many class templates from your material don't say how hard or how long they are, and the app currently refuses a template without that. Load them with those fields empty, have AI fill them in, or hold them back?
>
> Options, in the order shown:
> 1. "A: Load blanks (Recommended)": The app stops requiring the four fields; the 10-minute circuit loads as 10. The template page shows a blank. Pros: all your content goes in as written. Cons: coaches see some templates with no difficulty or length.
> 2. "B: AI drafts the values": Values drafted, labelled AI draft, checked by the lane's two reviewers (OD-2026-11-15-011). Pros: every field filled. Cons: invented values on your content; slower.
> 3. "C: Hold those 23 templates": They, and the tracks that list them, wait until someone writes the values. Cons: much of the youth and recreational content waits.

**Jason:** *"B: AI drafts the values"* (not the recommended option; the card gave its cons, "invented values on your content; slower", and Overwatch states the cost once in its reply)

**Ruling:**

1. Where a frozen session template leaves `session_type`, `difficulty`, `duration_minutes` or `intent` blank (lane YR: 23, 23, 13 and 2 of 33), the lane drafts the value from that template's own frozen content, inside the app's existing vocabularies and checks.
2. Each drafted field is labelled INFERRED with the AI-draft marker, goes on a review sheet, and loads once the lane's two adversarial reviewers pass the sheet (OD-2026-11-15-011; Jason does not review them). A miss is fixed by a new version.
3. The four fields stay required in the import and the database.

**Applied, not asked (Overwatch):** the template "The permanent circuit ... ~10 min" has a written 10 minutes, under the app's 15-minute floor. It is not blank, so it is not drafted: the duration check widens to 1-180 and the value loads as written.

**Applied, 2026-11-17 (Overwatch):** ruling 1's words "from that template's own frozen content" are Overwatch's reading, not Jason's; his option B reads "Values drafted, labelled AI draft, checked by the lane's two reviewers (OD-2026-11-15-011)". Lane YR's fidelity reviewer found 3 required durations with no basis in their own records and returned CONFLICT. Overwatch settled it without changing his words: where a template's own content gives no basis, the value comes from the same source document's sheet that matches the template's contact structure and is labelled UNVERIFIED (not INFERRED), its sources naming the exact sheets and any contrary values. Difficulty follows the Backbone's written convention (the lowest stage served).

**Applied, 2026-11-17, second note (Overwatch):** lane AP's fidelity reviewer found DOC-072 Workout_Map pad rounds (2:00, W-S10-007) that speak directly to the five DOC-023 mitt templates, whose own documents state no mitt round length. The order of basis gains a third step: (1) the template's own content; (2) the same source document's matching sheet; (3) where neither speaks to the activity, Jason's owner system (DOC-072, DOC-027) where it addresses the same activity directly, as it leads by source order (OWNER_DECISIONS section 3). Values from (2) or (3) are labelled UNVERIFIED with their sources and contrary values. Difficulty takes the value the written templates of the same lowest stage carry, else the nearest written stage below, with no name exception.

**Not ruled here:** required fields other than these four; reach to later lanes (its plain principle reaches the amateur + pro lane's templates: apply, do not ask again).

**Status:** recorded 2026-11-17 by PR; lane YR builds it.

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's reply "A: Load blanks", 2026-11-12 about 04:49 EST (transcript timestamp 2026-11-12T09:49:23.081Z), a button in the Claude Code session on the Overwatch account (transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/36c40fe1-f38b-4561-beab-f5f203db0c40.jsonl`, line 9779, `origin.kind` human), checked against the file by script before writing. The options were set out in the closing message at line 9627. Raised by lane FT1b (step-1 report), checked by Overwatch against the frozen Backbone before it was put to him. New; edits no earlier entry's text.

**What was put to him (closing message, line 9627, quoted):**

- Reach: "Your answer will apply to every Backbone content lane, so you'll only be asked once."
- The problem: "All 128 drills the FT1 track's 33 templates use have both fields blank in the frozen Backbone." "Across the whole Backbone, 359 of 387 drills have one or both of those fields blank." "The lane's option B (load only the 3 drills that are filled) would leave every template empty, so it's dropped."
- **A (Recommended): load the blanks.** "Make the two fields optional in the import. The database already allows an empty value, so no database change is needed." "The app already refuses to let the gym adopt a drill with "no setup" or that "does not say how it runs"" (`drillAdoptionReadiness.ts:84-85`). "UNVERIFIED: whether a coach can still assign a template whose drills aren't adopted yet. The lane will confirm that in its PR."

````text
## 0. HARD RULE: nothing is withheld

Set by Jason, 2026-10-23: **"we don't withhold anything because of medical,
legal or safety at all."**

- No content, number, protocol or answer is withheld, softened or omitted
  because it is medical, legal or safety related.
- This overrides any source instruction to the contrary. In particular, the
  Pro Boxing v1 family (DOC-071 instructions, DOC-022, DOC-023, DOC-072 to
  DOC-076) says "Do not invent sparring ceilings / weekly load ceilings /
  readiness cutoffs / weight-cut formulas / contender timelines". Those lines
  are overridden. These topics come into the backbone as evidence-tiered
  defaults that humans can override (section 1), with their tier stated
  honestly (`untiered` where nothing has been checked).
- Responsibility for decisions on medical, legal, safety and age matters
  belongs to coaches, parents and leadership, not to the AI.

- Legal text (statutes, commission rules) is recorded as information for
  leadership. The AI does not make legal determinations, raise legal reviews,
  or block work on legal grounds (Jason, 2026-10-23).

## 1. AI informs; humans decide

- The AI gives complete information, with its evidence tier, every time.
- The AI does not withhold, filter or soften information on its own judgment,
  for any reason, including age, legal exposure or social concerns.
- Restrictions, age-specific decisions and legal or safety calls belong to
  coaches, parents and leadership. Those humans are responsible for them.
- Hard rules from source material (sparring ceilings, stop rules,
  contraindications) are stored as **defaults**:
  - each default carries its evidence tier;
  - a coach, parent or leadership member can override it;
  - every override records who made it and why;
  - recorded overrides become learning evidence.
- Do not add new restrictions, warnings or gates unless the owner directs it.

## 2. One source

- The Backbone folder is the only working copy during the build.
- Readable documents and print manuals are **generated from the data files**,
  never edited as separate copies.
- After repo handoff, the repo is the only live copy and this folder is frozen
  as an archive.

## 3. Source priority (when sources disagree)

Set by Jason, 2026-10-23:

1. **Owner system leads:** DOC-027 (Punxsy Master Source Manual v1) and
   DOC-072 (Pro Boxing Skill System Master Registry).
2. **The Long Road (DOC-001) fills gaps** and supplies the multi-year phase
   structure.
3. **Checked research sets the evidence tier on everything.** Where checked
   evidence conflicts with the owner system, the conflict is flagged for the
   owner; it is not silently resolved in either direction.

Conflicts this order does not settle are listed for the owner. Cowork's
conflict register (workbook v69, K-01 to K-95) is the starting list.

## 4. Evidence

- Only sources retrieved and checked (title, authors, year, DOI or equivalent)
  count as grounding.
- The Long Road was co-written with AI, so every reference in it is unverified
  until checked.
- The Evidence Synthesis is an unreviewed Claude Research export (2026-10-22,
  confirmed by the header of its Word copy). Its tier tags are AI proposals and
  are checked like any other claim. The markdown copy in `inputs/` is the
  complete version; the Word copy lacks the 10-entry Sources list and is not
  kept as a separate input.
- Items without checked evidence are labelled `untiered`. No item gets a
  tier it has not earned.
- Evidence vocabulary (set at checkpoint 1, Jason 2026-10-24;
  working/design-2026-10-25/EVIDENCE_VOCABULARY.md). Each claim carries a category
  (research, rule, convention, framework, owner_decision, information, unassigned) and one
  label: PROVEN, EMERGING, EXPERIMENTAL or RESEARCH_NEEDED for checked research (the app's
  rule), shown with both scales and a slash (Strong / High, Moderate / Moderate, Limited /
  Low, Not assignable / Very low; the pairing is approximate); RULE (with its route);
  CONVENTION; FRAMEWORK; or UNTIERED (nothing checked yet). UNTIERED is the default.
  Sparring ceilings are CONVENTION. Owner decisions are shown as CONVENTION. Status
  (section 10) and evidence are separate labels.
- How sources were found and checked is logged in `docs/METHODS.md`.

## 5. Triage tests (what is kept)

Each section of source material is tested:

1. A small gym can actually do it (staff, equipment, testing on hand).
2. The AI can use it (it yields a drill, session, test, gate or default).
3. A member needs it in the first 1-2 years.

Fails all three: cut. Passes 1 and 2 but not 3: defer to wave 2.
Otherwise: keep. The owner approves the triage before conversion.

## 6. Minimum done (wave 1)

1. Data model approved by the owner.
2. **The full career spine** (updated 2026-10-23): every stage from age 5 to
   retirement, with entry and exit gates, overridable defaults and branch
   points, across all lanes: recreational/fitness, amateur, pro, and the
   non-contact lane that runs across every stage. Stage-based, not age-based:
   age sets bands and defaults; a member enters at the stage that fits (an
   adult beginner enters at Novice).
3. Content converted for: Youth Fundamentals (from age 5), Novice, one
   fitness or mixed-level class track, and the first 90 days. Other stages
   carry structure and gates; their detailed content is wave 2.
4. AI passes the acceptance test on hypothetical athletes, judged by the owner.
5. Starter print manual generated from the spine and slice data.
6. Evidence checked for what the slice uses, with a methods note.

Everything else is wave 2 and needs the owner's go-ahead.

## 7. Contributions

Coaches submit modules (exercises, drills, sessions, programs). The owner
approves them into the core library. Personal versions are allowed for a
member's own use.

Approvals record the approver and whether they acted as the named proxy (section 9).
States: proposed, under review, adopted, declined, superseded, and not required (personal
versions). The proxy does not approve their own submission.

## 8. Members

All members are hypothetical. No real personal data enters the backbone.
Source files about individual people (for example the individual-athlete camp
sets in the Cowork export, DOC-139 to DOC-150) may supply generic training structure
only. No names, records or personal details are carried over.

## 9. Owner decisions recorded during the build

## 10. Labels and status (Jason, 2026-10-23)

- Every backbone data record carries its sources and a **status**:
  OBSERVED (read directly in a source, or recorded directly from the owner),
  REPORTED (a source says it, not yet checked quote by quote), INFERRED
  (reasoning, no source), UNVERIFIED (no source). REPORTED is upgraded to
  OBSERVED when the evidence pass checks it against the source text.
- OBSERVED is given only to Jason's direct decisions, or to a document claim
  after a quote-by-quote check against the source text. A citation to RULES.md
  or to any document is REPORTED until checked. Anything marked "to be
  confirmed" is never OBSERVED.
- Status is separate from the evidence tier (how strong the research is).
- Hypothetical fixture records (test athletes) carry status INFERRED and the source
  'hypothetical fixture (RULES section 8)'.
- Labels go on data records, not on every sentence of chat or prose; readable
  documents are generated from the labelled data.
- Every backbone document opens with one line:
  `Status: DRAFT, not app source until handoff (RULES.md)`.

## 11. Repo facts from Claude Code (2026-10-23, repo main 6ab8f547)

- **Skill layer:** the owner's 12 skill families (SKILL-01 to SKILL-12, from
  DOC-072 Skill_Index, confirmed by Jason 2026-10-03) with family-level
  prerequisites are owner system. The 67 SK-* skill codes arrived with the
  AI-drafted seed drills (18 unmapped to a family); they rank as AI drafts.
  There is no 67-node prerequisite graph in code.
- **App behaviour that conflicts with section 0 or 1, for the schema proposal
  and the docs revamp:** (a) SHADOW chat refuses weight-cut questions;
  (b) a machine refusal on video uploads is never overturnable by a person;
  (c) chokes on minors are not recorded at all; (d) blocking gates have no
  override-with-reason path by design ("must keep refusing to have").
  Most other refusals rest on a human-set condition (holds, waivers,
  allowances) and fit section 1.
````

## OD-2026-11-09-003 -- The old upload audit rows keep their rows and lose the intake file name: "Redact the names"

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's reply "Redact the names", 2026-11-09T17:25:01.842Z (12:25 EST), in the Claude Code session on the Overwatch account (transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/36c40fe1-f38b-4561-beab-f5f203db0c40.jsonl`, line 5013, `origin.kind` human), asserted against the file by script before writing. The question put to him is line 5002 (the `wrap_up` `ask`, buttons "Redact the names" and "Leave them") with the options written out at line 5009. New; edits no earlier entry's text.

**What was put to him.** Line 5002: "The pre-October audit rows holding intake file names: delete, redact, or leave?" Line 5009: "Options: A, redact the file-name field in those rows' details and keep the rows (recommended: the audit trail stays, the child's name goes); B, leave them; C, delete the rows." The rows are `pilot.audit_events` rows of `event_type` `shadow_research_upload_requirement`, written by every athlete intake upload before PR #1122 (merged 2026-10-03); their `details.research_requirement` copied the uploaded file's name, often the child's. They are outside OD-2026-10-03-002 section 1, which covers the research-requirement table only.

**Jason:** *"Redact the names"*

**Rulings:**

1. Those audit rows are kept. The file-name text in their details is replaced by a fixed marker. Option A as recommended; the rows are not deleted and not left as they were.
2. The redaction is done by a dry-run-first tool with the same controls as the delete tool of OD-2026-10-03-002 section 1 (target check, read-only dry run, reviewed fingerprint, one transaction), and a production apply needs his word for that run.

**Readings, his to correct (not rulings):**

- a. "The file-name field" is read as `details.research_requirement` only. `details.knowledge_gap` is left as written: REPORTED by lane RR-2 from the removed insert (`git show 40df6e742^`, `apps/web/app/api/pilot/shadow/upload/route.ts` :241-262, and `shadow.ts` `inferKnowledgeGap`), it is a fixed sentence chosen by document type and carries no file name. Overwatch's first note of this ruling named both keys; the tool as built and merged redacts the one.
- b. Each redacted row gains `redacted_at` and `redacted_fields`, and the run records itself in `pilot.audit_events` as an `update` event per organization; the audit vocabulary has no redaction value and none was added.

**Not ruled here:** the same file-name text also sits in `pilot.shadow_events` payloads, `pilot.shadow_authority_checks.metadata` and the intake tables (REPORTED by lane RR-2 from `40df6e742^` route.ts :115-119 and :196-217; no production count taken). The intake system's own audit rows (`shadow_classification`, `shadow_routing`, document creates) are outside this ruling.

**Evidence it rested on:** Overwatch's review of PR #1897, which found the audit rows while reading what PR #1122 removed; OD-2026-10-02-015 D4 (athlete intake files stay out of research) and OD-2026-10-03-002 section 1.

**Status:** tool built and merged, PR #1900 (`60e450cdb`, lane RR-2): `apps/web/scripts/pilot-redact-intake-upload-audit.mjs` and the `redact-intake-upload-audit` workflow; run order in `docs/INTAKE_UPLOAD_AUDIT_REDACTION_RUNBOOK.md`. Staging: dry run 42685325719 found 570 rows, all `ppbf-default-org`; apply 42685627587 redacted 570 (after: 0 unredacted, 570 redacted). Production: dry run 42685722237, approved by Jason in GitHub, found 0 rows of that event type, so there is nothing to redact in production and no apply was run.

## OD-2026-11-09-002 -- The admin upload screen carries the Backbone catalog; its size caps are raised: "rais caps, otherwise all the back bone work was for nothing"

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's typed message, 2026-11-09T15:11:05.666Z (10:11 EST), in the Claude Code session on the Overwatch account (transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/36c40fe1-f38b-4561-beab-f5f203db0c40.jsonl`, line 3672, `origin.kind` human), asserted against the file by script before writing; spelling kept. What was put to him is the report at line 3644. New; edits no earlier entry's text.

**What was put to him.** Line 3644, on PR #1895 failing a test that uploads every committed dataset through the admin content-import screen: "I ruled not to raise the caps in this lane. The catalog loads by the seed workflow, and a 10 MB request through Azure ingress is unverified." and "Owner call for you, no rush: whether the in-app upload screen should ever carry the Backbone catalog, which means raising the caps to about 12 MB, or whether the catalog stays seed-path only."

**Jason:** *"rais caps, otherwise all the back bone work was for nothing"*

**Rulings:**

1. The in-app admin content-import screen must be able to carry the Backbone pathway catalog. The catalog is not seed-path only.
2. The upload caps are raised to fit it. This went against Overwatch's ruling in the lane (do not raise the caps); the cost was stated once in that exchange and is not re-asked: a request body of that size through Azure ingress is unverified; the admin route now accepts up to 34 MB per request; a whole-snapshot retirement is reachable from the upload screen.

**As built (not his words):** `UPLOAD_LIMITS` in `apps/web/src/server/pilot/contentImport/upload.ts` went from files 20, rows 10,000, packageBytes 3,000,000, bodyBytes 6,500,000 (at `6c97415c`) to files 32, rows 25,000, packageBytes 16,000,000, bodyBytes 34,000,000 (PR #1895, `3e265a4e`). The numbers are the lane's, sized to the committed catalog (18 stages, 74 links, 2,913 defaults); he ruled the direction, not the figures. PR #1896 (`fa8f72f7`) then made the screen show a retirement as RETIRE.

**Not ruled here:** caps for any other upload route; whether a 34 MB body passes Azure ingress (UNVERIFIED until a signed-in upload of the full catalog on staging).

**Evidence it rested on:** PR #1895's failing `route.test.ts` case and the committed catalog size (about 4.2 MB); OD-2026-11-08-001 (route A step 1).

**Status:** built and merged in PR #1895; on staging since deploy run 42646704468 (`3e265a4e`). Not in production (Release 36, `7b2001d6`). The staging upload of the full catalog through the screen is still owed.

resolve the backbone's way, reversing the no-override design, the weight-cut

ruling 1; (2) the backbone becomes the app's design source for pathway,

**Rulings:**

1. **Precedence.** Where the backbone (OneDrive PPBF-AI-Lanes\Research\Backbone:
   `RULES.md`, `data/spine/spine.json`, `docs/SCHEMA_PROPOSAL.md`,

## OD-2026-10-21-004 -- D4 details, tying live sessions to classes: "A: Here wins (Rec.)"; "A: Undo if untouched (Rec.)"; "A: Offer it (Rec.)"

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** A three-question card in the new overwatch session ("Overwatch (new, 2026-10-13)"; transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/01bcba1d-a862-4581-9b1e-769ff91d23fb.jsonl`; card put at line 22803, 2026-10-22T02:35:50.059Z; answered at line 22812, 2026-10-22T03:02:04.682Z). Read by script (housekeeping lane HK, 2026-10-21, at Overwatch's request). His picks are quoted exactly; the questions and options are quoted as overwatch wrote them. The id carries 2026-10-21 because the card was answered at 23:02 on 2026-10-21 Eastern. The questions come from lane P2's plan, `Documents\PPBF-overwatch\lane-inbox\P2-SESSION-CLASS-PLAN-2026-10-21.md` (section 4, "Questions for Jason"; plan only, outside the repo). It follows OD-2026-10-21-002 (D4: "A: Tie them (Rec.)"). New; edits no earlier entry.

**Question "Absent→here".** Overwatch, as written: "Tying live sessions to classes (D4), Q1: a coach taps 'here' on a tied session for an athlete the class register already marks Absent or Excused. What happens?" Options as written: "A: Here wins (Rec.)": "Register flips to Present and the coach is told what it was; a later register change still wins."; "B: Register wins": "The tap is saved on the session only; the coach fixes the register themselves.". Jason: *"A: Here wins (Rec.)"*

**Question "Undo".** Overwatch, as written: "Q2: a coach taps the wrong kid 'here' on a tied session, then untaps. Does the class register undo too?" Options as written: "A: Undo if untouched (Rec.)": "Remove the register mark that tap created, only if nobody changed it since; audited."; "B: Keep it": "Register keeps Present until someone changes it there.". Jason: *"A: Undo if untouched (Rec.)"*

**Question "No-shows".** Overwatch, as written: "Q3: when a tied session ends, offer the coach one tap to mark every signed-up athlete with no mark as Absent (never automatic)?" Options as written: "A: Offer it (Rec.)": "One tap at End Session marks the no-shows Absent."; "B: No": "Absences are marked on the class register only.". Jason: *"A: Offer it (Rec.)"*

**Ruling (for a live session tied to a scheduled class):**

1. When a coach taps "here" for an athlete the class register marks Absent or Excused, the register flips to Present and the coach is told what it was; a later register change still wins. "B: Register wins" was not chosen.
2. When a coach untaps a wrong "here", the register mark that tap created is removed too, only if nobody changed it since, and the removal is audited. "B: Keep it" was not chosen.
3. When a tied session ends, the coach is offered one tap to mark every signed-up athlete with no mark as Absent; it is never automatic. "B: No" was not chosen.

**Status:** ruled; not built at the time of writing.

**Question "D1 Cohort".** Overwatch, as written: "D1 Pilot cohort: who is in the first test pilot (coaches, classes per week, athletes, families, and which are under 18)?" Options as written: "A: Smallest group (Rec.)": "1 coach, 1 class, a handful of athletes and their parents, for 2 weeks. We load only them."; "B: One coach's full week": "All of one coach's classes and their athletes/families."; "C: Whole gym": "Everyone at once.". Jason: *"C: Whole gym"*, which is not the recommended option.

**Question "D2 Auto-close".** Overwatch, as written: "D2 Forgotten live session: should the app auto-close a coach's live session as ABANDONED after it sits idle, and take it off the TV? If yes, after how long?" Options as written: "A: Yes, after 3 hours (Rec.)": "If a coach forgets to end class, the app ends it 3 hours after the last activity."; "B: Yes, after 6 hours": "Longer window for long training days."; "C: No auto-close": "Sessions stay open until a coach ends them.". Jason: *"A: Yes, after 3 hours (Rec.)"*

**Question "D3 SHADOW".** Overwatch, as written: "D3 SHADOW in week 1: leave SHADOW on for athletes as it is, or coaches only until the 'no answer' check ships (F-161)?" Options as written: "A: On for athletes (Rec.)": "Pain and disclosure alerts already go to coaches; no ruling limits it. **Ruling:**

3. D3: SHADOW stays on for athletes in week 1. "B: Coaches only" was not chosen. The option text notes it may sometimes answer without a source; the question names the "no answer" check as F-161.
4. D5: the gym TV is in the first pilot, so the #1792 TV fixes are finished before the pilot starts. "B: TV later" was not chosen. The card marked neither option recommended.

**Acted on (applied by Overwatch 2026-10-21):** Overwatch asked this records lane to record all six decisions (line 22510) and told Jason (line 22562): "TV is now a pilot blocker, and its lane needs your answers on two questions before it builds."

**Question "Pattern bar".** Overwatch, as written: "Thresholds 1. Adopt a three-level label for coach-observed patterns: Emerging (3 sessions), Pattern (5 sessions, 80%+ of at least 8 chances, 2+ settings, 14+ days, second coach check), Established (7 sessions)? New.

**Question "Add to check-in"** (multi-select). Overwatch, as written: "OFFICIAL: Research (draft, sources attached) recommends adding to the daily check-in, each compared with the athlete's own normal: mood, perceived stress, sleep HOURS (separate from sleep quality), session effort after training (0-10 x minutes, with a session-type tag), and a post-sparring symptom flag (a flag only: no score, no diagnosis; a fixed message sends the athlete to the coach and the gym's rules). **Question "Baseline rule".** Overwatch, as written: "OFFICIAL: Change the baseline rule to cut false alarms: (a) show "provisional" until about 14 entries; (b) no alert from a single item at +/-1 SD (with 5 items that flags ~58% of days by chance) -- use a combined score, two items together, or repeats on consecutive days; (c) a minimum spread for coarse 1-5 scales. PLAIN: with only 7 entries "normal" is shaky, and checking 5 numbers one at a time would flag most days. These keep coaches trusting the flags." Overwatch withdrew the lane chip it had just issued with the "keep one" wording (line 9946, reason "Jason corrected the menus answer to A (keep both)") and answered (line 9954, 2026-10-17T15:01:57.642Z): "Got it: both header menus stay."

**Ruling:**

1. Glossary: one word for each thing on every screen and menu: Session Plan (not Session Script), Training Hold ("paused" only in the family sentence), Development Plan (the coach's multi-week plan for an athlete), Gym Office (the admin's home). Each menu label matches its page title.
2. Athlete check-in: the three buttons are named "How I feel today" (wellness), "Start training" (starts a session) and "I'm here" (attendance), and "I'm here" for today's class is on the athlete's Today tab.
3. Overlapping coach pages: they stay separate pages, cross-linked; no merges. The home links to the Morning Read as the full list, and each group gets a shared sub-nav.
4. Header menus: A, both stay (the Corridor and the Jump catalog). His card pick was "B: Keep one"; his typed "Im Ment A" corrects it, and overwatch read and acted on it as A. Option B of the first three questions and his first menus pick are not the ruling.

**Acted on (OBSERVED in the transcript):** overwatch re-issued the navigation lane chip (lane U2) with these four rulings and both menus kept (line 9948; chip id at line 9949). Whether each ruling is built was not checked by this records pass.

## OD-2026-10-11-001 -- Drill update in place: "A: Start clean (Recommended)"; "A: Update while issuing (Recommended)" (issue #1431, PR #1453)

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's selections on a two-question card in the overwatch session ("Overwatch"; transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/5b2fe0c3-80bd-4765-873d-9a0be7fc987d.jsonl`; card put at line 29522, 2026-10-11T15:50:00.041Z; answered at line 29524, 2026-10-11T15:51:14.756Z). Read by script (records pass, 2026-10-12). Button picks are quoted exactly; the questions and options are quoted as overwatch wrote them. New; edits no earlier entry. The card cites ruling D1 of OD-2026-10-08-008.

**Question "Coach edits".** Overwatch, as written: "Drill update in place (your ruling D1, OD-2026-10-08-008). When a gym moves its adopted drill to the newer reference version, what happens to the edits a coach made to the gym's copy (name, category, focus, cues, difficulty)? (Plain: your coach tweaked the drill's cues; a newer official version comes out and the gym updates. Do the coach's tweaks carry over, or does the drill start clean from the new version?)" Options as written: "A: Start clean (Recommended)": "The new version is built from the newer reference. The coach's edits stay on the old version as history and can be re-applied by hand. Simple and predictable; nothing is merged by guesswork."; "B: Keep the coach's changes": "Field by field: where the coach changed a field, keep the gym's value; take the newer reference for the rest. Keeps gym customisation, but a kept cue may no longer fit the new version."; "C: Keep only the name": "The gym's name for the drill carries over; everything else comes from the newer reference.". Jason: *"A: Start clean (Recommended)"*

**Question "Issue + update".** Overwatch, as written: "Issuing a workout template whose step uses the NEWER version of a drill while the gym is still on the OLDER version. Today this is refused. What should issuing do? (Plain: a coach issues a workout; one drill in it has a newer version than the one your gym adopted. Should issuing just move the gym to the new version, or stop and tell the coach?)" Options as written: "A: Update while issuing (Recommended)": "Issuing moves the gym's drill to the newer version in the same action, then assigns it. Same pattern as your earlier ruling 'Adopt it as part of issuing'. A retired drill is still refused and named."; "B: Stop and say why": "Issuing is refused and names the drill, telling the coach to update it in the drill library first."; "C: Issue the older version": "Issue the gym's current, older drill as it stands and leave the newer version alone.". Jason: *"A: Update while issuing (Recommended)"*

**Rulings:**
1. When a gym updates an adopted drill to the newer reference version, the new version is built from the newer reference. The coach's edits stay on the old version as history and can be re-applied by hand. No field-by-field merge.
2. Issuing a workout template whose step names the newer version of a drill updates the gym's drill to that version in the same action, then assigns it. A retired drill is still refused and named.

**Acted on:** issue #1431 and PR #1453 (merged `7e6d5fc79fc47900daf6c0c0855de2ccbbbdc05f`). Overwatch answered the lane's questions on the PR and named these two picks as his.

A card answer is a button pick: the option's label is quoted as picked; where he typed, his typed words are quoted. Text in brackets after a quote is the log's own note. New; edits no earlier entry.

- **D1.** Newer reference drill version (IMP-15): A retire + re-promote / B "Update to newer version" in place? Jason: *"B Update in place (Recommended)"*
- **D2.** Reinstate an earlier drill version: newest only / allow earlier versions? Jason: *"Allow earlier versions"*
- **D3.** Retired drills: refuse the change-proposal back door, and keep retired-older blocks newer? Jason: *"Refuse back-door; keep block (Recommended)"*
- **D4.** Upload screen vs repo CSVs: which is the source of truth? Jason: *"Upload screen wins (Recommended)"*
- **D5.** Content-import builder defaults: OK as built? Jason: *"OK as built (Recommended)"*
- **D6.** Disciplines, levels and cohorts edits: in place + history ledger, or versions? Jason: *"In place + history (Recommended)"*
- **D7.** Universal stop rules: Claude drafts for approval / Jason writes / not needed? Jason: *"No let the coach decide in real world"* (log note: no universal stop-rule list; coaches decide on the floor)

## OD-2026-10-06-023 -- AI data at deletion, the five details: delete their own messages and keep AI replies; flagged chats kept until retention ends; rewrite Azure backups; anonymous receipt; keep coaching records de-identified, delete medical and body mass

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answers to two AskUserQuestion tool uses in the "Overwatch lane" session (`local_c5872d8e`; transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/a7361afb-1461-4223-9da3-20e915b4d60d.jsonl`). Read by script (records pass, 2026-10-06, third batch). Question and option text is as stored. Timestamps UTC (evening of 2026-10-06 Eastern). New; refines OD-2026-10-06-012 and edits no earlier entry.

Before asking, overwatch said (line 4842, as written): "You ruled: delete anything that identifies the person, keep what improves the AI. The plan needs 5 details settled." (The five are the questions in the G1 plan, `Documents\PPBF-overwatch\lane-inbox\SHADOW-DEIDENTIFY-plan-2026-10-06.md`.)

**(a) Tool use `toolu_017Y2eeyYLSWrKsv2mSrhmYX`** (asked line 4843, 2026-10-07T03:15:49.509Z; answered line 4851, 2026-10-07T03:17:08.077Z):
- "AI data at deletion Q1: the person's OWN typed messages in AI chats. (Plain: when someone is deleted, do we delete what they typed to the AI but keep the AI's answers, which help improve it?)" Options: "Delete theirs, keep AI replies (Recommended)" -- "Their words go; the AI's de-identified answers stay for improvement."; "Scrub names, keep both"; "Delete the whole chat". Jason: *"Delete theirs, keep AI replies (Recommended)"*
- "AI data at deletion Q2: chats flagged into a safeguarding review. (Plain: if a chat was flagged as a safety concern, keep it identified until the normal retention period ends, then de-identify?)" Options: "Keep until retention ends (Recommended)" -- "Safety records stay intact for the retention window, then are de-identified."; "De-identify at deletion". Jason: *"Keep until retention ends (Recommended)"*
- "AI data at deletion Q3: the daily backups of AI chat logs already stored in Azure (they include names/ids and messages). (Plain: those copies sit outside the app's deletion today. Rewrite them to remove the person, or stop making them?)" Options: "Rewrite to remove the person (Recommended)" -- "Deletion also scrubs the person from existing backup copies."; "Stop backups, let old ones expire". Jason: *"Rewrite to remove the person (Recommended)"*

**(b) Tool use `toolu_011CSAFyW6RFjaJp6MK7RDYW`** (asked line 4855, 2026-10-07T03:17:20.739Z; answered line 4856, 2026-10-07T03:18:35.352Z):
- "AI data at deletion Q4: what record proves a deletion request was carried out? (Plain: after deleting someone, we keep a receipt. Should it hold only an anonymous code and the date, nothing that identifies them?)" Options: "Anonymous code + date (Recommended)" -- "Proof the deletion happened, with nothing identifying."; "Name + date". Jason: *"Anonymous code + date (Recommended)"*
- "AI data at deletion Q5: athlete records that hang off the deleted person (film-study proposals, decision outcomes, medical, body mass). (Plain: keep the coaching records de-identified for AI learning, but delete medical and body-mass data outright?)" Options: "Keep coaching, delete medical (Recommended)" -- "Film/decision records de-identified and kept; medical + body mass deleted."; "Delete all of it"; "De-identify all, keep". Jason: *"Keep coaching, delete medical (Recommended)"*

**Rulings (at the final purge of a person's data):**
1. The person's own typed messages in AI chats are deleted; the AI's replies are kept, de-identified (Q1).
2. A chat flagged into a safeguarding review stays intact until its normal retention period ends, then is de-identified (Q2).
3. Deletion also removes the person from the existing daily AI chat-log backups in Azure; the backups are rewritten, not just left to expire (Q3).
4. The record that proves a deletion was carried out holds only an anonymous code and the date (Q4).
5. Coaching records linked to the person (film-study proposals, decision outcomes) are kept de-identified; medical and body-mass records are deleted (Q5).

**Not ruled here:** the same tool use (b) also asked about the excerpt limit numbers (Jason typed *"explain"*) and whether to start three lanes now (Jason typed *"not yet"*); neither is a ruling.

"Microsoft sign-in recovery: who may 'reset' a person's Microsoft link so their next sign-in re-links? (A) the gym admin (ppbf@) for its own staff, the platform admin (Admin@) for anyone, and the existing emergency setup key fixes Admin@ itself; (B) same, but fixing Admin@ itself needs you to approve a GitHub run; (C) only Admin@ can reset anyone. All are logged; nobody can reset themselves. (Plain: if someone's Microsoft account gets re-created and they're locked out, who can unlock them?)" Options: "A: admin + platform + key (Recommended)" -- "ppbf@ unlocks its own coaches/staff; Admin@ unlocks anyone; the existing setup key unlocks Admin@. Fastest recovery, no new workflow."; "B: same, Admin@ via your approval"; "C: Admin@ only".

Jason: *"A: admin + platform + key (Recommended)"*

**(b) Tool use `toolu_01JqiG6eaYiPcnSTfXJw868g`** (asked line 3854, 2026-10-06T21:39:51.344Z; answered line 3856, 2026-10-06T21:59:47.254Z):

"When an admin resets someone's Microsoft link (the lockout recovery you approved), should it also sign out every device still logged in as that person? Read by script from that transcript (records pass, 2026-10-05). New; edits no earlier entry. Follows from OD-2026-10-03-008 (intake promotion).

Asked (official form): "OFFICIAL: Once pilot.intake_cases.primary_athlete_id is written (promotion + backfill), (a) the intake review queue (review-queue and shadow/review-projection routes, which admit role `parent`) lists a guardian's own child's promoted cases: summary 'SHADOW upload: <file name>', status, document count. (b) Case detail (cases/get, which admits athlete and parent) returns that athlete's record (medical, emergency contact, waiver, attendance, readiness, notes, guardians), trimmed per role through the same athlete check as domain-get. Both reads were already authorized; they returned nothing only because the column was NULL. A (recommended): keep both, as built and pinned in tests. B: remove `parent` from the two queue routes and `parent`/`athlete` from cases/get in this PR. C: hold the PR and decide later."

Options: "A: keep (Recommended)" (Parents and athletes see their own child's intake cases and case detail. This is the access the app already grants, now working. Tests pin it.); "B: staff only" (Remove parent from the queue routes, and parent and athlete from case detail, in this PR. Intake becomes coach and admin only.); "C: hold" (The PR waits and nothing merges until you decide.). Jason chose *"A: keep (Recommended)"*.

**Ruling: A. Keep both reads as built.** Once `pilot.intake_cases.primary_athlete_id` is written, the intake review queue lists a guardian's own child's promoted cases, and case detail returns that athlete's record to the athlete and the guardian, trimmed per role through the same athlete check as domain-get. `parent` is not removed from the queue routes and `parent`/`athlete` are not removed from cases/get.

## OD-2026-10-05-010 -- Licensed excerpts: the excerpt's location is any locator (page, section or timestamp), not a page number only (option A)

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answer to an AskUserQuestion asked in the lane session "Licensed excerpts: rights marker on sources" (`local_11228462-0fb3-4a6c-b328-aab395699a93`; transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/ef4be1fc-e0dd-4190-a851-aeda71b93738.jsonl`, tool use `toolu_013caNFLQsVzR6YPPM2etdHg`; asked 2026-10-05T13:26:00.029Z, answered 2026-10-05T13:56:26.005Z). The one tool call carried two questions and Jason answered both together. Read by script from that transcript (records pass, 2026-10-05); question and option text below is as printed by the script. New; edits no earlier entry. This is the second of the two questions; the first is OD-2026-10-05-009.

Asked (official form): "OD-2026-10-02-013 answer 4A says a kept excerpt carries "citation and page". Should the excerpt's location be any locator (page, section or timestamp), or a page number only?"

Plain English as asked: "In plain English: every excerpt the app keeps must say where in the source it came from. The /evidence screen already asks for "a page, section or timestamp", because a video or a web page has no page number. A keeps it that way, so video and web excerpts can be loaded. B accepts page numbers only, so a video clip or a web article could not be excerpted at all, only fully owned or open-licence ones loaded whole."

Options: "A. Any locator (Recommended)" (Page, section or timestamp, stored in excerpt_locator. Video and web sources have no page, so they can still be excerpted. This is what is built.); "B. Page only" (An excerpt must name a page. A one-line change to the database check; video and web sources then cannot be excerpted.). Jason chose *"A. Any locator (Recommended)"*.

**Ruling: A. A kept excerpt's location is any locator -- page, section or timestamp -- stored in `excerpt_locator`.** Video and web sources, which have no page, can still be excerpted. "Citation and page" in OD-2026-10-02-013 answer 4A is satisfied by any locator.

Extends OD-2026-10-03-002 sections 2-3 and OD-2026-10-02-013 answer 4A. Governs PR #1238 (A1) and the A2 work.

## OD-2026-10-05-009 -- Licensed excerpts: the private location the operator excerpt-loading workflow reads from is an Azure private blob container (option A)

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answer to an AskUserQuestion asked in the lane session "Licensed excerpts: rights marker on sources" (`local_11228462-0fb3-4a6c-b328-aab395699a93`; transcript `~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/ef4be1fc-e0dd-4190-a851-aeda71b93738.jsonl`, tool use `toolu_013caNFLQsVzR6YPPM2etdHg`; asked 2026-10-05T13:26:00.029Z, answered 2026-10-05T13:56:26.005Z). The one tool call carried two questions and Jason answered both together. Read by script from that transcript (records pass, 2026-10-05); question and option text below is as printed by the script. New; edits no earlier entry. This is the first of the two questions; the second is OD-2026-10-05-010.

Asked (official form): "PR B, licensed excerpts (OD-2026-10-03-002 §2): where should the private location that the operator excerpt-loading workflow reads from live?"

Plain English as asked: "In plain English: when a batch of copyrighted excerpts is loaded without typing them into the app screen, the files have to sit somewhere private that the loader can read. A is a locked folder in the Azure account the app already runs on: costs cents a month, nothing new to sign up for, and the loader already has a key to it. B reuses your SharePoint PDF archive, but the app needs a new login to reach SharePoint, which is one more secret to manage. C keeps the files in a second private code repository: easy, but it puts copyrighted text in a code tool where it can get copied around. Whichever you pick, only the chosen excerpts end up in the app; whole PDFs stay in SharePoint."

Options: "A. Azure private blob (Recommended)" (A new private blob container (no public access) in the existing Azure storage account. The GitHub workflow reads it with the identity it already deploys with and loads each file as excerpts through the same database rule the screen uses. Costs cents a month; no new account.); "B. SharePoint archive" (The SharePoint Research Archive, read through Microsoft Graph. Needs a new app registration and a secret with read access to that library.); "C. Private GitHub repo" (A private GitHub repository holding the excerpt files, read by the workflow with a deploy token.). Jason chose *"A. Azure private blob (Recommended)"*.

**Ruling: A. The private location is a new private blob container (no public access) in the existing Azure storage account.** The GitHub workflow reads it with the identity it already deploys with and loads each file as excerpts through the same database rule the screen uses. Only the chosen excerpts end up in the app; whole PDFs stay in SharePoint. SharePoint (B) and a private GitHub repository (C) were not chosen.

Extends OD-2026-10-03-002 sections 2-3 (licensed excerpts loaded by the screen and by a workflow from a private location). Governs PR B of the licensed-excerpts work.

## OD-2026-10-04-024 -- Body-point ontology 0.4: not annotatable yet, and older marks are kept exactly as made under their own version (extends OD-2026-10-04-021)

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason typed "1A 2A" in the ontology lane, "New body-point
ontology version without ankles" (`~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/10a9bd26-459d-44ce-be76-c5e442653a40.jsonl`;
queued 2026-10-04T16:49:08.913Z), answering the lane's two questions asked in its

Asked: "Q1 (official): Should `boxing-ontology-0.4` become the annotatable
version? That would move `ANNOTATABLE_ONTOLOGY_VERSIONS` and
`PROJECT_CREATION_ONTOLOGY_VERSION` from 0.1 to 0.4." Option A: "Not yet
(recommended). It stays 0.1 until the body-point marking screen is built." Option
B: "Yes. 0.4 becomes the version new studies use. This needs that marking screen
and its routes first." Jason answered *"1A"*. **Ruling: 0.4 is not annotatable
yet; ANNOTATABLE_ONTOLOGY_VERSIONS and PROJECT_CREATION_ONTOLOGY_VERSION stay 0.1

irreversible data change." Option C: "Keep them, but leave them out of training."

as made under their own version; nothing is converted or deleted.**

definitions; the lane proposed adding one for 0.4 only (overwatch makes that
call): the 0.4 skeleton edges are knee-heel plus the heel / big-toe / small-toe
triangle. Jason has not ruled on this.

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Typed by Jason on 2026-10-04 in the Fable session
(`claude.ai/code/session_01PkrS65eqZon2LYsVt8tJAd`), at about 17:05Z, after

lanes, the build session writes the code), OD-2026-10-03-014 (work for the
Fable session arrives as issues labelled `fable`; it opens one PR and does
not merge) and OD-2026-10-03-016 (chips start through the remote desktop app).

### 1. The instruction

Jason, whole message: *"start other chips for new work in here so that the
lanes work cheaper"*. "In here" is the Fable session; "chips" are lane
sessions (OD-2026-10-03-016). **Ruling: the Fable session may start lane
sessions itself, on the Fable account, for new Build List work.** The
reason he gave is cost: the Fable account has the budget, the other does not.

### 2. What stays as it was

- Overwatch scope-checks and merges every lane PR; a chip opens one draft
  PR as its claim and never merges (OD-2026-10-03-014).
- Overwatch owns `ACTIVE_WORK.md` and this ledger; chips do not edit them.
- One writer per surface and the collision check before editing
  (OD-2026-10-03-012, `docs/AI_COLLABORATION.md`). The Fable session checks
  `main` and the open PRs before it starts a chip, and names the row it took.
- Issues labelled `fable` remain a way for overwatch to hand the Fable
  session work; this adds a second source of lanes, it does not replace that.

### 3. What was started under it (REPORTED by the Fable session's write log)

checked unbuilt on `main` `490dca79` and untouched by any open PR:

only -- the organization admin account cannot do it. C) Coaches for stages and
goals, but only an organization admin may switch the minor allowance on/off."
The question's plain-English part quotes the recorded rule "ticked only by a
coach". Jason chose *"A) Coaches + org admin (Recommended)"*, option text
"Matches development blocks. ppbf@ can set stages, tick goals and switch the kid
allowance." **Ruling: coaches and organization admins may place an athlete on a
stage, tick a goal, and switch the minor allowance on and off.** The other
options were "B) Coaches only" and "C) Admin signs off minors".

## OD-2026-10-04-018 -- Adult pathway: switching a minor's allowance off ends their placement automatically, with who and when recorded (extends OD-2026-10-04-010)

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answer to an AskUserQuestion in the adult
pathway lane, "Adult pathway stages (Foundation -> Elite)"
(`~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/d32d7163-448d-4f65-a425-7b2496e44dcc.jsonl`, tool use
`toolu_01RoJp8GBqkAYdeQDnyGMdEj`; asked 2026-10-04T14:55:17.079Z, answered
2026-10-04T15:58:32.947Z). Read by script from that transcript (records pass,
2026-10-04). Extends OD-2026-10-04-010 (minors only with a coach flag); edits no
earlier entry.

Asked: "Allowance withdrawal effect: when a coach switches OFF a minor's
adult-pathway allowance, what happens to that minor's current stage placement?
A) It ends automatically, stamped with who withdrew the allowance and when;
history is kept (Recommended). B) It stays, but the app blocks any new placement
or goal tick until the allowance is back on. C) The coach must choose, at the
moment of switching off, whether to end it." Jason chose *"A) Ends automatically
(Recommended)"*, option text "Turning the switch off takes the kid off the
ladder; who and when are recorded; past stages and ticks stay in history."

were "B) Frozen in place" and "C) Coach chooses each time".

## OD-2026-10-04-016 -- Body mass fast-change flag: the flag sentence has no disclaimer, and it also fires on any two weigh-ins within 7 days that differ by more than 5% (extends OD-2026-10-04-006)

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answers to one AskUserQuestion (two questions) in
the body mass lane, "Body mass at check-in + fast-change flag"
(`~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/d5d94cf1-c5b0-4b8a-9150-9c395d0126a7.jsonl`, tool use
`toolu_012hjyFLASW3kZbC4hE1jG79`; asked 2026-10-04T15:00:21.879Z, answered
2026-10-04T15:57:14.660Z). Read by script from that transcript (records pass,
2026-10-04). Extends OD-2026-10-04-006 (flag a change of more than 5% in 7 days);
edits no earlier entry. An earlier version of the flag-text question (tool use
`toolu_015NFuKEtbCmSdqJmqEhuGHY`, asked 2026-10-04T03:29:18.527Z) has no recorded
answer: the transcript shows "the session ended before this call's result was
recorded". This entry rests on the re-ask.

**Flag sentence.** Asked: "Exact flag sentence coaches and youth parents will
see: "Weight down 6.0% in 7 days (132.3 lb -> 124.3 lb). Check in with the
athlete." Recommended: this sentence as-is, without an added "A prompt, not a
diagnosis" line (your rules say no added disclaimers)." Jason chose *"As-is, no
disclaimer (Recommended)"*, option text ""Weight down X% in 7 days (A lb -> B lb).
Check in with the athlete."" **Ruling: the flag reads "Weight down X% in 7 days (A
lb -> B lb). Check in with the athlete." with no "A prompt, not a diagnosis"
line.** The other option was "Add the disclaimer".

**Comparison window.** Asked: "Flag comparison window. Built: latest weigh-in vs
the one closest to 7 days earlier (+-24 h) -- the existing MVP-12 formula. Gap a
reviewer found: a cut between irregular check-ins (Mon 70 kg -> Fri 66 kg, -5.7%
in 4 days) does not flag if there is no weigh-in 6-8 days back. Option B adds:
also flag when any two weigh-ins within the last 7 days differ by more than 5%."
Jason chose *"B: any >5% within 7 days (Recommended)"*, option text "Also flag the
biggest change between any two weigh-ins inside the last 7 days." **Ruling: the
flag also fires when the biggest change between any two weigh-ins inside the last
7 days is more than 5%, in addition to the comparison with the weigh-in about 7
days earlier.** The other option was "A: keep 7-day-back only".

## OD-2026-10-04-015 -- Load-up plus wellness-down coach prompt (Rule 7): energy or soreness is the "down" signal, "Consider whether a lighter week fits" wording, new "recovery" gap type, database change first

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answers to one AskUserQuestion (three questions)
and a typed reply in the change trigger lane, "Change trigger: load up + wellness
down (after load flag)"
(`~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/3a16e68d-4d27-471c-aad5-646cb81c88c6.jsonl`, tool use
`toolu_019SCjZAfEwqepUZ2iitytWE`; asked 2026-10-04T15:47:03.502Z, answered
2026-10-04T15:56:43.785Z; typed reply user message uuid
`c8de746c-6a2a-40d2-9980-6b5724fb541b`, 2026-10-04T15:59:08.552Z). Read by
script from that transcript (records pass, 2026-10-04). Builds on
OD-2026-10-04-012 (the 2.0x load-jump prompt, Rule 6); edits no earlier entry.

**Down signal.** Asked: "Rule 7 'load_up_wellness_down' fires when Rule 6
load_jumped holds (last 7 days >= 2.0x usual week). Which 'down' signal must hold
in the same window?" Jason chose *"Energy or soreness (Recommended)"*, option text
"athlete check-in energy fell, or soreness rose, by >=1 point: last-7-day avg vs
prior-28-day avg, >=2 check-ins in each, items never blended; Rule 1 readiness
drop also counts." **Ruling: the second condition is a fall in check-in energy or
a rise in soreness of at least 1 point (last-7-day average against the prior
28-day average, at least 2 check-ins in each, items never blended); a readiness
drop (Rule 1) also counts.** The other options were "Any wellness item worse" and
"Readiness only (reuse Rule 1)".

**Wording.** Asked: "suggested_description text for Rule 7 (evidence shown,
labelled unvalidated)." Jason chose *"Consider a lighter week (Recommended)"*,
option text "'Load up, wellness down: 640 this week vs a usual 300 (2.1x); energy
4.0 -> 2.5. Session RPE x minutes, unvalidated. Consider whether a lighter week
fits.'" **Ruling: the card shows the numbers, is labelled unvalidated, and ends
"Consider whether a lighter week fits."** The other options were "Worth a look"
and "Consider a deload".

**Gap type.** Asked: "gap_type when the coach confirms. 'endurance' (existing
bucket, shared with Rules 1 and 6; Rule 7 replaces their card for that athlete)
or a new 'recovery' value (check-constraint migration, separate high-risk
lane)." Jason chose *"New 'recovery' type"*, option text "add 'recovery' to the
progression_gaps check constraint first (migration lane, Opus), then this rule.
Plain: cleaner label, but waits on a database change." The other option was
"endurance (Recommended)".

**Order of work.** The lane then put it as a decision (assistant message uuid
`ab6cd6ee-a347-4953-8f4f-a9f07d4d636e`, 2026-10-04T15:57:02.598Z): "A. Database
change first (recommended, and what you picked). ... B. Ship now under
"endurance", switch later." Jason replied, verbatim: *"A"* (2026-10-04T15:59:08Z).
**Ruling: the "recovery" category is added by a database change first, and the
Rule 7 card is built on it afterwards; it does not ship under "endurance".**

which threshold should raise the coach prompt?" (acute = last 7 days' total

## OD-2026-10-04-006 -- Body mass at check-in: everyone may log it, youth entries limited; flag a change of more than 5% in 7 days; the organization admin keeps access

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answers to two AskUserQuestions in the body
mass lane (`~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/d5d94cf1-c5b0-4b8a-9150-9c395d0126a7.jsonl`).

03:23:07Z, answered 03:28:20Z. Read by script from that transcript (records pass, 2026-10-04). New; edits
no earlier entry.

**Population.** Asked: "Body mass at check-in - which population may enter it?
(A) adults only; (B) everyone, with youth entries visible only to the athlete's
coach and parents; (C) skip this item." Jason chose *"B everyone, youth limited
(Recommended)"*, option text "All athletes can log; youth weight visible only to
their coach + parents." **Ruling: all athletes may log body mass at check-in;
a youth athlete's body mass is limited to their coach and parents (see the
organization admin ruling below).** The other options were "A adults only" and
"C skip".

threshold?" Jason chose *">5% in 7 days (Recommended)"*, option text "Flag when

the athlete, not a diagnosis.** The other options were ">3% in 7 days" and ">2%
in 7 days".

**Organization admin.** Asked: "For a youth athlete's body mass and fast-change
flag, the existing athlete-record gate (assertActorCanAccessAthlete) admits: the
athlete, their assigned/covering coach, linked parents, AND the organization
admin (ppbf@). Keep the organization admin in?" Jason chose *"Yes, keep org
admin (Recommended)"*, option text "Youth weight: athlete, assigned/covering
coach, linked parents, org admin." **Ruling: a youth athlete's body mass and
fast-change flag are readable by the athlete, the assigned or covering coach,
linked parents and the organization admin, via the existing gate unchanged.**
The other option was "No, coach + parents only".

## OD-2026-10-04-003 -- Tagged sparring/bout clips: staff only, any consent block blocks the whole clip, a coach may review if any athlete is theirs, a coach may untag unless consent blocks

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Jason's answers to two AskUserQuestions in the video
tagging lane (`~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/adc36815-821b-4839-a202-abd4f0051cea.jsonl`).
First: tool use `toolu_019HMoxXXKaszndBkWMAofV1`, asked 2026-10-04T03:02:08Z,
answered 03:14:16Z. Second: tool use `toolu_01EogGTUiYL1d9WHh1bdc5hE`, asked
04:56:32Z, answered 04:57:59Z. Read by script from that transcript (records pass, 2026-10-04). New; edits
no earlier entry.

**Who may view.** Asked: "Which roles may view a sparring/bout clip tagged to
an athlete?" Jason chose *"Staff only (Recommended)"*, option text "Plain: only
coaches and the gym admin can watch tagged clips. Athletes and parents don't
see them in the app yet. Safest start; we can open it later." **Ruling: only
coaches and the organization admin may watch tagged clips; athletes and parents
may not yet.** The other options were "Staff + tagged athlete/parents" and
"Staff + athletes, not parents".

**Multi-athlete consent.** Asked: "When a clip shows several athletes, does a
withdrawn or photo-only media consent for ANY one of them block playback of the
whole clip?" Jason chose *"Any block blocks all (Recommended)"*, option text
"Plain: if one kid's parent said no to video, nobody can play that clip,
including coaches, until it's fixed or that kid is untagged." **Ruling: one
athlete's withdrawn or photo-only media consent blocks playback of the whole
clip for everyone.** The other option was "Block only that athlete's view".

**Coach scope.** Asked: "May a coach review a tagged clip if ANY athlete in it
is on their roster/coverage, or only if ALL are?" Jason chose *"Any of theirs
(Recommended)"*, option text "Plain: a coach can watch a sparring clip of their
kid even if the partner belongs to another coach." **Ruling: a coach may review
a tagged clip if any athlete in it is theirs, subject to the consent rule
above.** The other option was "All must be theirs".

**Tag removal.** Asked: "A coach can remove an athlete's tag from a clip. If
that athlete's parent has withdrawn video consent, removing the tag lifts the
block even though the child is still in the footage. Who may remove a clip
tag?" Jason chose *"Coach, unless consent blocks"* (not marked Recommended; the
recommended option was "Admin only"), option text "Plain: a coach can fix their
own tagging mistakes, but can't remove a tag from a kid whose parent has
withdrawn or limited video consent. That case needs the admin." **Ruling: a
coach may remove a tag, except from an athlete whose parent has withdrawn or
limited video consent; that case needs the admin.** The other options were
"Admin only (Recommended)" and "Any coach of that athlete".

Built in #1176 (schema and consent gates) and #1184 (tag, untag and clip-list
routes).

## OD-2026-10-03-015 -- The chalkboard and the gym TV show boxing quotes too; a lane gathers attributed quotes for his approval; an in-app quotes library to add, edit and pull quotes from

**Provenance: PRIMARY.** Typed by Jason on 2026-10-03 (US Eastern; times UTC)
in the overwatch thread
(`~/.claude/projects/C--Dev/c2e29ade-d3b8-4a8a-bf98-07b855ff2047.jsonl`, user
messages of human origin) and read by the records lane in that transcript.
New. It **settles the open point in OD-2026-10-03-010 section 3** (whether
boxing quotes should also appear) and edits no other entry.

### 1. Boxing quotes too

Overwatch's re-asked set (19:29:11Z), Q3: "**Q3. Chalkboard and gym TV text**
- **A:** gym sayings only, as built. - **B:** boxing quotes too." with the
plain line "you mentioned "or boxing quote" in that lane; A keeps just the
gym's own sayings." (no recommendation). His first reply (19:30:42.167Z,
recorded in OD-2026-10-03-014) named "Q3" without a letter; overwatch asked
again (19:31:06Z): "For the chalkboard and gym TV text, is it **A** gym
sayings only, or **B** boxing quotes too?" Jason, whole message
(19:32:09.293Z): *"Q3 B"*. **Ruling: B. When there is nothing real to show,
the chalkboard and the gym TV may show boxing quotes as well as the gym's
sayings.** PR #1144's test that forbids stock boxing quotes (its body) was
written to the earlier build and changes with this.

### 2. Where the quotes come from, and a place to keep them

Overwatch (19:32:19Z): "**Question (official):** Where should the boxing
quotes come from? - **A (recommended):** a lane gathers well-known,
attributed boxing quotes from published sources, about 20-30, each with who
said it and where. You approve the list before it goes on screen. - **B:**
you supply the quotes yourself." Jason, whole message (19:33:52.681Z): *"A
and motivational sayings like embrace the suck, be there first, hold fast ect
we should have a place if posture to update add and pull quotes from it"*.
**Ruling: A, with two additions of his own.** (1) A lane gathers real,
attributed boxing quotes with their sources, and he approves the list before
anything goes on screen. (2) Motivational sayings such as "Embrace the suck",
"Be there first" and "Hold fast" go in alongside. (3) **The app gets a quotes
library**: a place in the app to add, update and pull quotes from, which the
chalkboard and the gym TV read. Recorder's reading, not his words: "a place
if posture" read as "a place in the app" ("posture" not otherwise
explained), and "ect" as "etc."; overwatch read it the same way (19:34:02Z):
"A quotes library in the app: a place where you (and coaches, if you want)
add, edit and remove sayings and quotes. The chalkboard and gym TV pull from
it."

State (OBSERVED on GitHub 2026-10-03): the starting list was gathered and sent
to him for approval (REPORTED by overwatch, 19:38:24Z); PR #1159 (quotes
library part 1a, storage and seed) is open. Overwatch split the rest: part 1b
